changelog: Core Principles: Added an explicit instruction to avoid committing to agents/polarity/heads until clause-final disambiguators appear — to prevent premature assertions seen in critic cases.

When to Segment: Strengthened surface-cue guidance to treat noun phrases, names, numerals, and quoted strings as risky until their disambiguators (case particles, counters, closing quote, verb/predicate endings, name components) appear; made these positions candidates but lower-confidence.

Never Segment: Added absolute prohibition against splitting a noun and an immediately following numeral/counter sequence, and clarified not to split when that would produce a bare, unrenderable fragment that needs a following predicate.

Priority Rules: Deprioritised boundaries right after the Japanese comma '、' more strongly and lowered confidence for very-early boundaries unless sealed; added explicit high-risk categories (numeric quantifiers, partial names, quoted fragments) to be ranked last unless disambiguator present.

Decision Procedure: Made the two-step workflow explicit and added concrete disambiguator checks (case particles, closing quote, name delimiter, numeral/counter, sentence-final predicate) that automatically push a candidate into a lower-confidence bucket; required explicit cautious handling when a cut would finalize an agent, polarity, or head.
